title: UBC International Scholars Program
program_type: University need-and-merit scholarship awarded to nominated international entrants through a separate application administered by the UBC International Student Initiative
funding_type: Need-and-merit-based university scholarship; value commensurate with assessed financial need and, for the Vantage One Excellence Award, up to the full cost of the academic programme plus living costs (university- and donor-funded)
administering_authority: The University of British Columbia — UBC International Student Initiative (Undergraduate Programs and Admissions), with UBC Vantage College recommending the Vantage One Excellence Award
implementing_agency: UBC International Scholars Program team (international.awards@ubc.ca) and the UBC Scholarships portal operated on SurveyMonkey Apply; UBC Undergraduate Admissions evaluates the separate admission application
programme_action: UBC International Scholars Program — four award categories: Karen McKellin International Leader of Tomorrow Award; Donald A. Wehrung International Student Award; International Impact Award; Vantage One Excellence Award
description: The UBC International Scholars Program is the University of British Columbia's need-and-merit-based award programme for international students entering a first undergraduate degree directly from an accredited secondary school. Nominated applicants are automatically considered for four award categories — the Karen McKellin International Leader of Tomorrow Award, the Donald A. Wehrung International Student Award, the International Impact Award, and the UBC Vantage One Excellence Award — with each award's value determined by the recipient's documented financial need. Applicants must first be nominated by a high school or registered non-profit organisation, apply for admission to UBC, and then complete a separate award application through UBC's scholarship portal. An applicant who applies to the programme is not considered for UBC's merit-based entrance awards.

award_types: Karen McKellin International Leader of Tomorrow Award
Donald A. Wehrung International Student Award

award_types_detail.Karen McKellin International Leader of T: Recognises exceptional prospective international undergraduates who demonstrate superior academic achievement and exemplary leadership skills that support and empower others through collaboration, empathy and active listening, with positive impact through school and community service and notable achievement in academic or extra-curricular pursuits.
award_types_detail.Donald A. Wehrung International Student: Recognises outstanding international undergraduate students from impoverished or war-torn areas who have achieved academic excellence under challenging circumstances and who would be unable to attend university without significant financial assistance; students should demonstrate leadership potential and a strong commitment to making a positive impact in their communities.
award_types_detail.International Impact Award: Offered to exceptional students who have demonstrated leadership as well as commitment to and solutions for sustainability and climate change, natural resource conservation and management, social justice, equity and inclusion, or societal health and wellness; priority is given to first-generation learners and those from diverse lived backgrounds.
award_types_detail.Vantage One Excellence Award: Offered by UBC Vantage College for academically outstanding international students who do not yet meet the English Language Admission Standard for direct admission to UBC; awards range in value up to the full cost of a student's academic programme and living expenses, granted on the basis of academic merit with financial need also taken into account.

programme_structure.renewal_criteria: Awards are renewed for up to three additional years, or to degree completion, whichever is less. Vantage One Excellence Award recipients are reviewed annually to assess and update academic progress and financial need, and must maintain their status as an international student in Canada.

programme_duration.official_range: 4 years to degree completion; nominees' awards are renewable for up to three additional years; applicants entering through Vantage One add an 11-month first year before progressing into second year
programme_duration.renewal_note: Vantage One Excellence Awards are renewed for up to three additional years or to degree completion, whichever is less, with annual review of academic progress and financial need and a requirement to maintain international student status in Canada. Donald A. Wehrung awards were renewed for up to three additional years of undergraduate study or to degree completion, whichever is less, provided the recipient met UBC Senate renewal requirements, continued to demonstrate financial need and maintained a Canadian study permit.

funding.monthly_amount_note: UBC publishes no monthly stipend for the International Scholars Program. Award value is set per recipient by assessed financial need; the Vantage One Excellence Award ranges up to the full cost of the student's academic programme and living costs.
funding.living_allowance: Living costs are inside the award value (the Vantage One Excellence Award ranges up to the full cost of a student's academic programme and living costs), but no separate or itemised living allowance amount is published.
funding.travel_amount_note: Travel to Canada is not named as a covered benefit in the official award descriptions.
funding.institutional_costs: Covered — award value is determined by reference to UBC tuition and fees together with living and other related costs.
funding.fully_funded_note: Fully funded in the sense that the Vantage One Excellence Award ranges up to the full cost of a student's academic programme and living expenses; the other three categories are valued commensurate with documented financial need rather than at a published fixed amount. UBC does not publish the dollar value of any individual award, so no amount can be quoted.

tuition.conditions: Included in the award value; the value of each award is dependent on the recipient's financial need. The Vantage One Excellence Award ranges in value up to the full cost of the student's academic programme and living costs.

monthly_stipend.note: Not published in official source. UBC publishes no stipend amount for the International Scholars Program.

visa_support.note: Not published in official source. Recipients must hold a Canadian study permit; UBC publishes study-permit guidance separately.

insurance.note: Not published in official source as an award benefit. UBC requires all students to have basic and extended health insurance, budgeted by the student.

accommodation_support.conditions: Living costs are inside the value of the Vantage One Excellence Award (up to the full cost of the student's academic programme and living costs); the value is dependent on the recipient's financial need. No separate housing payment or amount is published. Scholars are advised to wait for award decisions before applying for residence — the first-year housing deadline is May 1, 2027.

bond.note: No service bond, repayment obligation or return-of-funds condition is stated in the official award descriptions. The only continuing conditions are annual review of academic progress and financial need, and — for the Vantage One Excellence Award — maintaining international student status in Canada.

total_estimated_value.note: UBC does not publish award amounts or a total value for the International Scholars Program; value is set individually by assessed financial need. For scale only, UBC states that it devotes more than $35 million CAD annually to awards, scholarships and other financial support for international undergraduate students; that figure covers all international undergraduate awards and must not be read as an individual award value.

final_year_condition: Not applicable as a bachelor's-completion question: the programme funds a first undergraduate degree and requires entry directly from an accredited secondary school, so final-year secondary-school students are the intended applicants. Applicants for the 2027 Winter session must have graduated from high school no earlier than June 2026, and nominees who have already entered or completed post-secondary schooling are not eligible for the Donald A. Wehrung International Student Award.
equivalent_degree_note: Yes — 'or equivalent standard' is applied to both the academic requirement (all As or equivalent) and the secondary credential. UBC publishes specific admission requirements for international high schools, the International Baccalaureate, Advanced Placement, British-patterned A-Level/GCSE, Indian CBSE/ISC curricula and other national curricula, and UBC Vantage College admits students below the direct-entry English standard.

eligibility.citizenship: Open to international students worldwide; the applicant must not be a Canadian citizen or permanent resident and will be studying in Canada on a Canadian study permit. Convention refugees and students intending to become landed immigrants to Canada are not eligible for the Donald A. Wehrung International Student Award.
eligibility.residence_requirement: Must hold or intend to hold a Canadian study permit and enter UBC directly from an accredited secondary school; no residence in Canada is required in advance.
eligibility.secondary_school_requirement: Entering UBC directly from an accredited secondary school. For the 2027 Winter session, applicants must have graduated from high school no earlier than June 2026. Grades 9–11 and Grade 12 interim/mid-year transcripts, plus predicted grades for courses in progress, are required.
eligibility.academic_requirements: Superior academic achievement — achieve all As or equivalent standard — in addition to meeting UBC's general and degree-specific admission requirements for the first-choice programme.
eligibility.gpa_requirement: All As or equivalent standard; UBC does not publish a single universal percentage cut-off and interprets the requirement against each applicant's curriculum.
eligibility.language_requirement: UBC's English Language Admission Standard (ELAS) for direct entry, by one of nine routes or an accepted test: IELTS Academic 6.5 with no part below 6.0; TOEFL iBT overall 90 (Reading 22, Listening 22, Writing 21, Speaking 21); PTE Academic overall 65 with 60 in each skill; Duolingo English Test overall 125 (Reading 115, Listening 115, Writing 120, Speaking 120); CAEL overall 70; Cambridge B2 First/C1 Advanced/C2 Proficiency 180; or the UBC Certificate in English Language (600). Applicants below the direct-entry standard may be eligible for UBC Vantage College and the Vantage One Excellence Award; Vantage One accepts a minimum TOEFL 70 and IELTS 5.5 with certain sub-scores. ISP applicants must meet the standard by January 31, 2027; test scores must be from January 1, 2025 onwards for the 2027/2028 Winter Session.
eligibility.extracurricular_requirement: Exceptional extracurricular activities and notable achievement in academic or extra-curricular pursuits are part of the programme's stated expectations.
eligibility.financial_need: A significant, documented level of financial need. UBC conducts a financial assessment that reviews documents outlining the family's gross income, expenses, family assets, dependants and annual school fees, and sources of financial support. It would be impossible for the applicant to pursue a UBC degree without meaningful financial help, the family cannot cover a significant level of the costs, and there is no access to external funding. The financial-need estimate is the amount of support the applicant requires to live and study at UBC after all resources are accounted for.
eligibility.previous_scholarship_restriction: Applicants may only be considered for either the merit-based or the financial need-based award programme. Applicants to the International Scholars Program are not considered for merit-based awards, including International Major Entrance Scholarships, the Outstanding International Student Award, Vantage One Entrance Awards and UBC Okanagan automatic awards consideration. A student may be nominated for only one award.
eligibility.enrolment_status_requirement: Must be applying for a first undergraduate degree and entering directly from secondary school. The applicant must apply for admission to UBC (myapplication.ubc.ca) before starting the award application, and the award application requests confirmation of the admission application. Students who have already entered or completed post-secondary schooling are not eligible for the Donald A. Wehrung International Student Award.
eligibility.field_restrictions: Not eligible for the UBC International Scholars Program awards: Bachelor of Nursing (Okanagan and Vancouver), Bachelor of Dental Science in Dental Hygiene, Bachelor of Medical Laboratory Science, Bachelor + Master of Management degree, dual degrees, joint degrees between UBC Okanagan and UBC Vancouver, and joint degrees with other post-secondary institutions. Applicants are considered for their first-choice programme and should still select a second choice.

academic_requirements.percentage_note: UBC states the requirement as 'superior academic achievement (achieve all As or equivalent standard)' rather than a single percentage; the standard is applied by UBC Admissions against the applicant's national curriculum or international programme.
academic_requirements.programme_specific_requirements: Applicants must also meet UBC's general and degree-specific admission requirements for the first-choice programme. Excluded degrees are Bachelor of Nursing (Vancouver and Okanagan), Bachelor of Dental Science in Dental Hygiene, Bachelor of Medical Laboratory Science, Bachelor + Master of Management, dual degrees, joint degrees between the two UBC campuses, and joint degrees with other post-secondary institutions.

academic_requirements.holistic_selection_note: Programme materials describe a holistic review of academic standing, leadership and community contribution, extracurricular achievement and documented financial need, with the programme's stated purpose of bringing together scholars from diverse countries and cultures. UBC publishes no numeric weighting.

english_requirement.moi_rule: English is the primary language of instruction. Nine alternative routes satisfy UBC's English Language Admission Standard (ELAS): four or more consecutive years of full-time study in English in Canada immediately before UBC or in a country where English is the principal language; 70% or better on the provincial examination portion of Alberta ELA 30-1 or BC English 12; AP English Language & Composition or Literature & Composition grade 4, or IB English A grade 5; an accepted proficiency test; six credits of transferable first-year English studies at a recognised university in an English-speaking country; graduation from a degree programme taught in English in a country where English is the principal language; four or more years at an eligible international secondary school in a non-English-speaking country; or the UBC Certificate in English Language (CEL) at Levels 600 and 650. Bilingual schools require an ELAS waiver request, and a waiver may also be requested for fully proficient applicants (due February 15, with a transcript and recommendation from an English teacher, guidance counsellor or principal emailed by the school).
english_requirement.test_score_note: Accepted tests and minimums (minimum applies to each part unless stated otherwise, in a single sitting; scores across multiple sittings cannot be combined): IELTS Academic 6.5 with no part below 6.0 (IELTS General, IELTS Indicator and IELTS One Skill Retake are not accepted); TOEFL iBT or TOEFL iBT Home Edition overall 90 with Reading 22, Listening 22, Writing 21, Speaking 21 (UBC institution code 0965); PTE Academic overall 65 with Reading 60, Listening 60, Writing 60, Speaking 60; Duolingo English Test overall 125 with Reading 115, Listening 115, Writing 120, Speaking 120; CAEL or CAEL Online overall 70; Cambridge B2 First, C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency 180; UBC Certificate in English Language (CEL) 600. Unlisted online tests (for example IELTS Indicator) may be considered only alongside a waiver request. Applicants for the 2027/2028 Winter Session must submit test scores from January 1, 2025 onwards, and International Scholars Program applicants must meet the standard by January 31, 2027.
accepted_tests: TOEFL iBT (including TOEFL iBT Home Edition)
Cambridge English Qualifications (B2 First, C1 Advanced, C2 Proficiency)

language_of_instruction.language_note: English is the primary language of instruction at UBC. UBC Vantage One offers Arts, Science and Applied Science (Engineering) tracks with integrated academic English over an 11-month first year, after which students progress into second year of their degree.

application_method.application_route: Apply for admission to UBC at myapplication.ubc.ca first, secure a nomination from a school or registered non-profit and a teacher referee, then complete the separate International Scholars Program application in UBC's Scholarship portal (SurveyMonkey Apply) at undergraduatescholarships.ubc.ca.
application_steps: 1. Mid-September — decide the academic programme and campus. You are considered for your first-choice programme, and you should still select a second choice.

2. Late September — discuss the nomination with your school. You need one nominator (guidance counsellor, principal, administrator or a registered non-profit acting as an educational institution) and one teacher referee, who must be different people. A high school or registered non-profit may nominate up to two students for UBC Vancouver (including Vantage College) and one student for UBC Okanagan.

3. Early October — apply to UBC for admission (the award application asks for confirmation and the EducationPlanner/UBC application reference number, so the admission application must be submitted first).

4. Early October — create an account on the UBC Scholarships application platform and invite your nominator and teacher referee to complete their forms; the award application cannot be completed until both are submitted. Both forms should be completed and submitted a few days before November 15.

5. Mid-October — gather family and financial information: annual income and expenses, family wealth and assets, dependants and annual school fees, sources of financial support, and a financial-need calculation using UBC's cost estimator; record extracurricular information and awards.

6. By November 15, 2026 (23:59 Pacific) — submit the completed application: nomination form, reference form, application form, programme of study, and essays and extracurriculars (four essay questions of roughly 150–250 words).

7. By January 31, 2027 — submit the admission documents requested in the 'Your UBC Application – Next Steps' email (transcripts, high school academic certificates, predicted grades) and meet the English Language Admission Standard; for ISP applicants this replaces the date in the email. UBC requires official transcripts and certificates from the award recipient and the school after selection.
8. January–March 2027 — complete the video interview if invited; you have one week to record your responses in the online application platform.

9. February–April 2027 — monitor email (mark UBC addresses as safe); award decisions are released on a rolling basis, and by early- to mid-April you are told whether you have received an award. Wait for the award decision before applying for residence — the first-year housing deadline is May 1, 2027.
application_method.application_fee: A separate award application fee is not published; applicants pay UBC's standard undergraduate admission application fee via the admission application. The current official page does not state any fee waiver for the 2027 cycle.

selection_process.weighting_note: UBC publishes no numeric weighting for the programme. Applicants do not select an award: UBC automatically considers each nominee for the awards they are eligible for.
selection_process.results_timing: Results are released on a rolling basis throughout February–April; by early- to mid-April, applicants are told whether they have received an award. Award offers for merit-based awards are usually issued before the admission acceptance deadline (most May 1).
selection_process.scholarship_rank_note: There is no applicant-chosen preference or ranking among the four award categories; the committee automatically considers each nominee for the awards they are eligible for, and the award value is set by assessed financial need.

degree_outcome.awarded_qualification: UBC bachelor's degree (first undergraduate degree) at UBC Vancouver or UBC Okanagan
degree_outcome.typical_programme_length: 4 years; 5 academic years where the student enters through the 11-month Vantage One first year
possible_awards: Karen McKellin International Leader of Tomorrow Award
Donald A. Wehrung International Student Award
degree_outcome.degree_note: Applicants are considered for their first-choice programme and should also select a second choice. The excluded degrees are Bachelor of Nursing (Vancouver and Okanagan), Bachelor of Dental Science in Dental Hygiene, Bachelor of Medical Laboratory Science, Bachelor + Master of Management, dual degrees, joint degrees between the two UBC campuses, and joint degrees with other post-secondary institutions. Successful Vantage One students progress into second year of their degree; a full-time international graduate of a UBC bachelor's programme can qualify for a post-graduation work permit of up to three years.
degree_outcome.credit_transfer: Vantage One carries the full requirements of the first year of an Arts or Science degree with integrated academic English, and students progress into second year on successful completion. UBC governs first-year credit from secondary credentials (IB, A-Levels, AP) separately from the award.

student_rights_and_cost_protection.tuition_fee_for_recipients: Recipients pay international tuition fees; the award is applied towards tuition and fees at a value commensurate with documented financial need, up to the full cost of the academic programme for the Vantage One Excellence Award. UBC determines international tuition by citizenship status, so awards are calibrated against the international fee schedule.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.application_fee_for_recipients: No fee waiver for the 2027 cycle is published on the current official International Scholars page. An earlier Donald Wehrung nomination package stated that DWISA nominees did not pay the UBC undergraduate application fee; that statement is not restated for 2027 and should be checked with international.awards@ubc.ca.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.student_agreement: Award winners' awards are reviewed annually to assess and update academic progress and financial need. Data submitted on the UBC Scholarships portal is collected under section 26(c) of the BC Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act (FIPPA) and handled within Canada by UBC and SurveyMonkey for the purpose of assessing suitability for awards.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.common_services: Recipients receive dedicated International Scholars Program advising, skill-building workshops and retreats, and access to standard UBC student services including the Applicant Service Centre, enrolment services, health and dental coverage, U-Pass transit access, housing, co-op and exchange.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_breach_consequence: No bond or repayment obligation is published. Continuing conditions are only annual review of academic progress and financial need and, for the Vantage One Excellence Award, maintaining international student status in Canada.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are not a Canadian citizen or permanent resident and will study in Canada on a study permit
Confirm you are entering directly from an accredited secondary school and graduated no earlier than June 2026
Check that your intended degree is not on the excluded list
Confirm your school can nominate you and has not used its two Vancouver or one Okanagan nomination slot
Decide your first-choice campus and programme, plus a second choice
Secure a nominator and a teacher referee who are different people, and give them your contact details and first-choice programme in late September
Complete the UBC admission application before starting the award application
Collect official family financial documents: income, expenses, assets, dependants' school fees, sources of support
Calculate your financial need using UBC's cost estimator
Book an IELTS, TOEFL, PTE, DET or CAEL sitting early enough for official results to reach UBC by January 31, 2027, with a test date from January 1, 2025 onwards
Draft four essays of roughly 150–250 words and compile extracurriculars and awards
Set your portal time zone to Pacific Time and submit before November 15, 2026 23:59
Submit transcripts and certificates by January 31, 2027, and check spam filters for UBC email
programme_comparison_fields: Award value and whether it is capped by assessed financial need or a fixed amount
Whether a nomination is required and the per-school nomination cap

practical_application_data.motivation_letter_strategy: Write four essays of roughly 150–250 words that give concrete evidence of leadership and community contribution rather than assertions: name the project, your role, what changed, and who benefited. For the Donald A. Wehrung award, make the circumstance and the academic achievement under that circumstance explicit. For the International Impact Award, anchor the essay to one of the stated themes (sustainability and climate change, natural resource conservation and management, social justice, equity and inclusion, or societal health and wellness) and say what you did about it. For the Vantage One Excellence Award, connect your academic and extracurricular record to your English-development plan in Vantage One.
profile_fit_labels: International student on a Canadian study permit
common_mistakes: Starting the award application before completing the UBC admission application — the award application asks for confirmation of admission submission
Assuming a self-nomination is possible; the school or non-profit must nominate, and there is a per-school cap
Leaving the nominator and referee forms to the last days — they must be completed before the November 15 deadline
Applying late in the window when the financial-need and essay sections are time-consuming
Applying to both this need-based programme and the merit-based entrance awards; only one stream is possible
Choosing an excluded degree (Nursing, Dental Hygiene, Medical Laboratory Science, Bachelor + Master of Management, dual or joint degrees)
Missing the document deadline of January 31, 2027 by following the date in the 'next steps' email instead
Applying for residence before the award decision; the first-year housing deadline is May 1, 2027

risk_flags.impact: No consideration for the 2027 cycle; the next opportunity is the September 2028 intake, opening early October 2027
risk_flags.mitigation: Start in early October, submit well in advance of November 15, and set the application time zone to Pacific Time

risk_flags.risk: Nominator or teacher referee submits late
risk_flags.impact: The award application cannot be completed or submitted even if the student's own sections are ready, because both forms must be submitted first
risk_flags.mitigation: Secure both forms in late September, invite them in the portal in early October, and follow up so they are completed a few days before November 15

risk_flags.impact: Applicants cannot know the dollar value in advance, so longer-term financial planning is uncertain and non-covered costs must be funded another way
risk_flags.mitigation: Treat the award as need-based and variable; use UBC's cost estimator to model the shortfall and prepare the financial documents that drive the assessment

risk_flags.risk: Applying also disqualifies merit-based award consideration
risk_flags.impact: An applicant who applies to the International Scholars Program is not considered for International Major Entrance Scholarships, the Outstanding International Student Award, Vantage One Entrance Awards or UBC Okanagan automatic awards, and may end up with nothing
risk_flags.mitigation: Decide deliberately between the need-based and merit-based routes using UBC's own guidance before applying, since only one stream can be pursued

risk_flags.risk: Intended degree is on the excluded list
risk_flags.impact: No eligibility for any award in this programme regardless of academic standing or need
risk_flags.mitigation: Check the excluded degrees (Nursing, Dental Hygiene, Medical Laboratory Science, Bachelor + Master of Management, dual and joint degrees) before selecting first and second choice programmes

risk_flags.risk: English Language Admission Standard not met by January 31, 2027
risk_flags.impact: The International Scholars Program application cannot proceed if documents or requirements needed for admission are missing
risk_flags.mitigation: Book an accepted test early enough for official results to reach UBC well before January 31, 2027, using a test date from January 1, 2025 onwards, or apply through the Vantage One route

risk_flags.impact: The award is not automatically continued; renewal depends on academic progress, continued demonstrated financial need and, for the Vantage One Excellence Award, continued international student status
risk_flags.mitigation: Maintain academic standing, keep financial documentation current for annual review, and retain study-permit status

risk_flags.risk: Vantage One pathway extends the degree by a year
risk_flags.impact: An 11-month Vantage One first year lengthens time and living-cost exposure beyond the standard four-year degree
risk_flags.mitigation: Compare the Vantage One fee and total cost against meeting the direct-entry English standard before choosing the route

database_notes: No substitution was required. The assigned target (Canada — UBC International Scholars Program, including the Donald A. Wehrung International Student Award and the Vantage One Excellence Award) is not on the DO-NOT-DUPLICATE list, Canada is an allowed region, and the award funds a first bachelor's degree.

The record covers the UBC International Scholars Program as a whole because the Donald A. Wehrung International Student Award and the Vantage One Excellence Award are award categories within it and cannot be applied for separately; applicants are automatically considered for the awards they are eligible for.

The award has no published dollar amount for any category, so monthly_amount, travel_amount, insurance, the tuition amount and total_estimated_value are all null. UBC publishes the Vantage One Excellence Award scale ('up to the full cost of the student's academic programme and living costs') but no maximum figure.

Deadline precision is 'exact': the live 2027 record on undergraduatescholarships.ubc.ca states 'Deadline Nov 15 2026 11:59 PM (PST)' and instructs applicants to set their application time zone to Pacific Time.

Research was performed on 2026-10-10 (the retrieval date). The SCHEMA_CONTRACT baseline date of 2026-10-03 was therefore superseded; this does not affect status, because the November 15, 2026 deadline is in the future either way and the application window opened October 5, 2026.

eligibility.previous_scholarship_restriction carries the rule that applicants may be considered for either the merit-based or the need-based award programme, not both, since the schema forbids an extra top-level key for it.

'ISP' is a short form used informally for International Scholars Program; UBC's own materials write the name out in full, so short_title should be read as a convenient abbreviation rather than an official acronym.

International Major Entrance Scholarship figures for Vantage One (up to $85,000 total; $25,000 first year and up to $20,000 for years 2–4) appear on the Vantage College awards page but are merit-based awards that International Scholars Program applicants are excluded from; they are deliberately not recorded as benefits of this programme.

The official_programme_guide_url is null: no 2027-cycle rulebook or handbook PDF is published on the official pages. A 2019–2020 Donald Wehrung nomination package exists at https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2018/10/2019-20-DWISA-Nomination-Package.pdf but is a superseded cycle document and was used only for document-format context.
UBC Vancouver (Vancouver campus) figures and the English Language Admission Standard table are campus-specific; the Okanagan campus has separate English requirements and award pages.

The logo asset was authenticated with an HTTP HEAD request on the official awarding domain (200, image/png, 2,825 bytes). The crest belongs to the University of British Columbia, which is the awarding body, so no third-party logo was used.
